source_boundary.preserved_question_intent: Explain how the Spring IoC container resolves supported singleton-bean circular references and the limits of that mechanism.

anchors: getSingleton early reference lookup and factory materialization

claims.text: Spring Framework can resolve some circular references by exposing an early reference to a singleton bean after instantiation but before full initialization/property population; constructor-to-constructor cycles remain unresolvable because the required instance does not yet exist and can produce BeanCurrentlyInCreationException.
source_anchors: one bean may be injected before full initialization

claims.text: The interview shorthand 'three-level cache' maps in current Spring source to singletonObjects for fully registered singletons, earlySingletonObjects for materialized early references, and singletonFactories for lazy early-reference factories. The factory level is important because it can defer creation of the reference until another bean actually needs it.
source_anchors: getSingleton early reference lookup and factory materialization

claims.text: During eligible singleton creation, AbstractAutowireCapableBeanFactory registers an ObjectFactory before dependency population. A dependent bean can call getSingleton for a bean currently in creation; the registry can invoke that factory once, move the result into the early-reference map, and later replace early state with the fully initialized singleton registration.
source_anchors: getSingleton early reference lookup and factory materialization

claims.text: Early exposure is not necessarily the raw object: getEarlyBeanReference delegates through SmartInstantiationAwareBeanPostProcessor instances, allowing infrastructure such as auto-proxy creation to provide an early wrapped reference. Spring also guards against inconsistent raw injection when the final bean is wrapped.

The early-exposure path is explicitly conditioned on singleton scope, allowCircularReferences and the bean being currently in creation; it is not a general algorithm that makes every constructor, prototype, proxy or arbitrary object-graph cycle valid.

writer_constraints: Treat '三级缓存' as interview shorthand for three singleton-exposure structures; do not claim Spring documentation formally defines all three as ordinary caches.
Explain the lifecycle ordering: instantiate -> register early-reference factory -> populate dependencies -> initialize -> publish final singleton.
Do not claim constructor-to-constructor cycles are solved by the three-level mechanism.
Do not generalize the singleton early-reference mechanism to prototype beans or every dependency graph.

Explain why singletonFactories exists instead of saying three Maps are needed only for performance: lazy early-reference creation also supports consistent early proxy exposure through SmartInstantiationAwareBeanPostProcessor.
Keep implementation statements version-bound to the checked Spring Framework main source because internal concurrency/locking details evolve.
Do not mix Spring Boot's application-level circular-reference defaults into the Spring Framework core mechanism unless explicitly marked as a separate product/version policy.
Do not recommend circular dependencies as design best practice; the official Framework API itself recommends refactoring rather than relying on them.
